title: Mathematics (math.*) weekly — 7 notable papers; latest announcement batch 11 November 2026 (window 7–13 November)
global_caveat: ArXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred ranking of notable recent papers, not a popularity list. Citation evidence for preprints this new is limited.

sections.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
sections.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, the authors show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension, disproving Guralnick's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct, for every fixed positive degree, faithful absolutely irreducible modules for finite simple groups whose cohomology dimensions grow without bound; the introduction gives an exact first-cohomology family for sufficiently large primes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The finite-group constructions use groups of type PSL over sufficiently large prime-power fields and faithful absolutely irreducible coefficients; the bounds are not uniform in a fixed characteristic.
sections.unique_caveat: The fixed-characteristic version remains open in the paper: it asks whether bounds may exist when the characteristic is fixed.

sections.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for SL_n(C)-Fock bundles
sections.abstract: Using cyclic Higgs bundles, the author disproves the conjecture that every SL_n(C)-Fock bundle has a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every rank n ≥ 3.
sections.claimed_result: At each rank n ≥ 3, universal existence and uniqueness cannot both hold: at a positivity wall either the required metric does not exist or nearby fields admit two distinct such metrics.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The construction uses cyclic Higgs bundles on closed oriented surfaces of genus at least two and the associated Fock fields and harmonic metrics.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem establishes a disjunction—failure of existence at the wall or failure of uniqueness just before it—rather than identifying which failure occurs in every instance.

sections.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
sections.abstract: The author rules out a 13-vertex simplicial triangulation of the three-torus using a g₂ lower bound, a reduction to a small simplicial complex, and fundamental-group and Alexander-duality arguments.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that no simplicial triangulation of T³ has 13 vertices; together with known bounds this leaves the minimum between 14 and 15.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns finite simplicial triangulations of the topological three-torus; the argument uses the Novik–Swartz g₂ inequality and a classification of fundamental groups of complexes on at most eight vertices.
sections.unique_caveat: It does not decide whether a 14-vertex triangulation exists, nor prove that the known 15-vertex construction is minimal.

sections.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
sections.abstract: For curves y² = φ_d(x) built from Chebyshev polynomials, the authors classify the prime-characteristic pairs and finite fields over which the curves are maximal, including a criterion for supersingularity in the case p ≡ 1 mod 4.
sections.claimed_result: For p not dividing 2d they determine all pairs (d,p) for which H_d is maximal over a finite extension of F_p, together with the fields; for odd d and p ≡ 1 mod 4, supersingularity is equivalent to maximality over an extension and occurs precisely for d = ℓⁿ with ℓ ≡ 1 mod 4 prime and p a generator modulo ℓⁿ.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: H_d is y² = φ_d(x), with φ_d(t+t⁻¹)=tᵈ+t⁻ᵈ; the stated classification excludes characteristics p dividing 2d.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated hypotheses exclude the ramified characteristics p | 2d; those cases are outside this classification.

sections.title: Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming in Polynomial Time
sections.abstract: The author gives a polynomial-time algorithm for two-stage mixed-integer quadratic programs with an arbitrary quadratic objective when the number of linking variables and each continuous block size are fixed, even as the number of blocks grows.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves polynomial-time solvability under fixed linking-variable count and fixed block size, with arbitrarily many continuous blocks and an arbitrary quadratic objective.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: All integer variables must be among the linking variables; continuous blocks interact only through those variables; linking-variable count and block size are fixed.
sections.unique_caveat: The polynomial-time guarantee is parameter-restricted; the author states the running-time exponent must depend on both fixed structural parameters unless FPT = W[1].

sections.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
sections.abstract: For C_h, the closure of nonreal roots of integer polynomials whose coefficients have modulus at most h, the author proves that C_h is connected exactly when h is pronic and gives component results at other heights.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves C_h is connected iff h=q(q−1); at every other height it has at least five components, with further results showing infinitely many components for broad ranges of nonpronic heights.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: C_h is formed from the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficient modulus at most h; connectivity changes if nonzero real roots are included.
sections.unique_caveat: Several explicitly listed small nonpronic heights are exceptions to the paper's general claim of infinitely many components, so component-count refinements depend on the particular height.

sections.title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
sections.abstract: The authors show that electrical positivity for circular planar networks and total positivity of associated symplectic matrices do not coincide, while deriving rational factorization-recovery formulas with uniqueness under nonvanishing conditions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the two specified notions of positivity do not coincide and give explicit rational formulas recovering factorization parameters from matrix entries and minors, with uniqueness under stated nonvanishing conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks and the associated positive Lagrangian Grassmannian construction.
sections.unique_caveat: The uniqueness statement is conditional on explicit nonvanishing requirements; the abstract does not claim a general factorization-recovery result outside those conditions.
